title: Orthogonal Uplift Learning with Permutation-Invariant Representations for Combinatorial Treatments
claim: A treatment's policy is embedded by summing probability-weighted atom representations, giving a permutation-invariant vector that plugs into an orthogonalized outcome model.
layout: 2 nested panels, bottom-to-top flow, blue arrow zooming into Treatment Net
description: A wide figure in a purple rounded frame titled "Permutation-invariant Orthogonal Uplift Learning (POUL)". The left panel shows the full model in three layers (Input, Model, Output). User features feed the baseline outcome, heterogeneity function and embedding propensity boxes. These sit inside a dashed box labeled Orthogonalized Uplift Learning, together with a blue diamond for the Treatment Net. Their outputs combine through subtraction, multiplication and addition nodes into the predicted outcome Y. A blue arrow leads from the diamond into a large blue-bordered right panel that expands the Treatment Net. In that panel, inputs T, s and a go through context and action embedding nets. The resulting φ(s,a) is multiplied by the policy probabilities Π(a|s,T) and summed over s and a, then passed through a linear net to give h(T). Pastel green, orange and yellow boxes mark the modules. Equations appear inside the boxes.
caption: Treatment Net: permutation-invariant embedding of combinatorial treatments. A treatment T is observed through its policy specification: for each context s ∈S (instantiated here as {s1, s2}), the treatment induces a distribution over atomic actions a ∈A (instantiated as {a0, a1, a2}). The network first learns embeddings for contexts and actions to form atom representations ϕ(s, a). These atoms are then reweighted by policy probabilities and aggregated via a permutation-invariant sum z(T), ensuring the representation depends only on the induced mixture. Finally, a learnable map produces the treatment embedding h(T), which is used by the orthogonalized uplift model (left panel) to estimate the causal effect τ(x).
abstract: We study uplift estimation for combinatorial treatments. Uplift measures the pure incremental causal effect of an intervention (e.g., sending a coupon or a marketing message) on user behavior, modeled as a conditional individual treatment effect. Many real-world interventions are combinatorial: a treatment is a policy that specifies context-dependent action distributions rather than a single atomic label. Although recent work considers structured treatments, most methods rely on categorical or opaque encodings, limiting robustness and generalization to rare or newly deployed policies. We propose an uplift estimation framework that aligns treatment representation with causal semantics. Each policy is represented by the mixture it induces over contextaction components and embedded via a permutation-invariant aggregation. This representation is integrated into an orthogonalized low-rank uplift model, extending Robinson-style decompositions to learned, vector-valued treatments. We show that the resulting estimator is expressive for policy-induced causal effects, orthogonally robust to nuisance estimation errors, and stable under small policy perturbations. Experiments on large-scale randomized platform data demonstrate improved uplift accuracy and stability in long-tailed policy regimes
